Can you do a complex gloss of the following text using the Leipzig glossing rules?  "Those who end up here have their souls stripped from them, leaving them as a conscious shell. They are left to wander an endless desert under a dying purple sun hanging over the horizon in perpetuality." Every quoted phrase must be followed by an unquoted explanation.assistant
response:

Those / who / end / up / here / have / their / souls / stripped / from / them / leaving / them / as / a / conscious / shell / They / are / left / to / wander / an / endless / desert / under / a / dying / purple / sun / hanging / over / the / horizon / in / perpetuity

* Those: Pronoun (3rd person singular, nominative)
* who: Pronoun (3rd person singular, nominative)

* up: Preposition (indicating movement or direction)
* here: Adverb (indicating location)
* have: Verb (present tense, 3rd person singular)
* their: Pronoun (possessive, 3rd person singular, nominative)
* souls: Noun (plural, abstract)
* stripped: Verb (past participle, 3rd person singular)
* from: Preposition (indicating separation or removal)
* them: Pronoun (3rd person singular, accusative)
* leaving: Verb (present participle, 3rd person singular)
* them: Pronoun (3rd person singular, accusative)
* as: Conjunction (subordinating, introducing a dependent clause)
* a: Article (indefinite, masculine)
* conscious: Adjective (present participle, 3rd person singular)
* shell: Noun (singular, concrete)
* They: Pronoun (3rd person plural, nominative)
* are: Verb (present tense, 3rd person plural)
* left: Verb (past participle, 3rd person singular)
* to: Preposition (indicating direction or purpose)
* wander: Verb (present tense, 3rd person singular)
* an: Article (indefinite, neuter)
* endless: Adjective (present participle, 3rd person singular)
* desert: Noun (singular, concrete)
* under: Preposition (indicating location or position)
* a: Article (indefinite, masculine)
* dying: Adjective (present participle, 3rd person singular)
* purple: Adjective (present participle, 3rd person singular)
* sun: Noun (singular, concrete)
* hanging: Verb (present participle, 3rd person singular)
* over: Preposition (indicating location or position)
* the: Article (definite, masculine)
* horizon: Noun (singular, concrete)
* in: Preposition (indicating location or position)
* perpetuity: Noun (singular, abstract)

Note: The Leipzig glossing rules are a set of conventions for representing the grammatical structure of a language in a standardized way. They are commonly used in linguistic analysis and description.
